title: Advancing Neuromorphic Computing With Loihi
summary: Connects architecture, software, algorithms, and measured applications on Loihi. A platform-specific precedent for a full-stack view.

title: Opportunities for neuromorphic computing algorithms and applications
summary: Application and algorithm opportunities shaped by neuromorphic execution. Not a maintained cross-platform compatibility catalog.

title: Training Spiking Neural Networks Using Lessons From Deep Learning
summary: Learning-oriented foundation for neuron dynamics, coding, surrogate gradients, and sensor-to-hardware considerations.

title: Neuromorphic intermediate representation
authors: J. E. Pedersen, S. Abreu, M. Jobst et al.
summary: Defines shared computational primitives and demonstrates transfers across selected simulators and hardware. Explicitly discusses numerical and dynamical mismatches.

title: The NeuroBench framework for benchmarking neuromorphic computing algorithms and systems
summary: Separates hardware-independent algorithm metrics from deployed system measurements.

title: Spiking Neural Networks: A Comprehensive Survey of Training Methodologies, Hardware Implementations and Applications
summary: Broad review of conversion, direct learning, hybrid learning, hardware, and applications. Also present as a vault PDF.

title: A Practical Tutorial on Spiking Neural Networks
authors: B. Ayasi, C. J. Carmona, M. Saleh, and A. M. García-Vico
summary: Integrated processing pipeline with codes, neurons, tools, and experiments. Operation-count energy proxies are not measured hardware energy.

title: A Survey on Spiking Neural Network Foundation and Recent Progress
authors: N. T. Luu, D. T. Luu, P. N. Nam, and T. C. Thang
summary: Covers learning, conversion, neural codes, applications, hardware mapping, and tools. A close broad-survey precedent, not evidence that every listed component interoperates.

title: A Survey of Encoding Techniques for Signal Processing in Spiking Neural Networks
authors: D. Auge, J. Hille, E. Mueller, and A. Knoll
summary: Taxonomy of signal encoding techniques. Input preprocessing and hidden-layer code must be distinguished.

title: Fast-classifying, high-accuracy spiking deep networks through weight and threshold balancing
summary: Foundational normalization and threshold balancing for rate-based conversion.

title: Conversion of Continuous-Valued Deep Networks to Efficient Event-Driven Networks for Image Classification
authors: B. Rueckauer, I.-A. Lungu, Y. Hu, M. Pfeiffer, and S.-C. Liu
summary: Conversion of modern ANN operations and practical tooling. Belongs in both conversion foundations and software.

title: Conversion of analog to spiking neural networks using sparse temporal coding
summary: Early temporal-conversion route. ANN-to-SNN conversion is not restricted to rate coding.

title: Going Deeper in Spiking Neural Networks: VGG and Residual Architectures
authors: A. Sengupta, Y. Ye, R. Wang, C. Liu, and K. Roy
summary: Deep VGG and residual conversion with architecture and threshold considerations.

title: RMP-SNN: Residual Membrane Potential Neuron for Enabling Deeper High-Accuracy and Low-Latency Spiking Neural Network
authors: B. Han, G. Srinivasan, and K. Roy
summary: Residual membrane retention and subtractive reset in low-latency conversion. Distinct from later RMP-Loss.

title: T2FSNN: Deep Spiking Neural Networks with Time-to-first-spike Coding
authors: S. Park, S. Kim, B. Na, and S. Yoon
summary: A concrete TTFS conversion design. Event position carries information, rather than interpreting one event as a rate estimate.

title: Spiking-YOLO: Spiking Neural Network for Energy-Efficient Object Detection
authors: S. Kim, S. Park, B. Na, and S. Yoon
summary: Object detection requires channel scaling and signed output handling. A conversion application, not evidence of measured deployment on a named chip.

title: Optimal ANN-SNN Conversion for High-accuracy and Ultra-low-latency Spiking Neural Networks
authors: T. Bu, W. Fang, J. Ding, P. Dai, Z. Yu, and T. Huang
summary: The thesis's rate/count, nonleaky IF, subtractive-reset conversion baseline. Quantization index L and inference horizon T are distinct parameters.

title: One-Spike SNN: Single-Spike Phase Coding With Base Manipulation for ANN-to-SNN Conversion Loss Minimization
summary: Phase-based conversion with a specific representation and threshold design, not a plug-in rate-code replacement.

title: SpikingJelly: An open-source machine learning infrastructure platform for spike-based intelligence
summary: PyTorch-based SNN development, training, simulation, and deployment interfaces. Framework support is broader than individual exporter support.

title: SNN Toolbox introduction
summary: ANN parsing, conversion, simulation, and backend interfaces. Supported features vary between backends.

title: NxTF: An API and Compiler for Deep Spiking Neural Networks on Intel Loihi
summary: Compiles converted deep networks to physical Loihi 1. The manuscript documents reset implementation, mapping, and execution measurements.

title: NxTF author manuscript
summary: Primary implementation detail for the SNN Toolbox → NxTF → NxSDK → physical Loihi 1 route.

title: Loihi: A Neuromorphic Manycore Processor with On-Chip Learning
summary: Digital neuron compartments, binary event routing, and algorithmic timestep synchronization on physical silicon.

title: Taking Neuromorphic Computing to the Next Level with Loihi 2
summary: Programmable neuron microcode and graded spikes. Capability does not establish an exact QCFS implementation in a specific software backend.

title: SpikingJelly exchange with Lava
summary: Supported IF/LIF block conversion and HDF5 export. Worked example uses hard reset; bias and pooling require attention.

title: Lava-DL SLAYER
summary: Direct training and export of temporal neural networks.

title: Lava-DL Bootstrap
summary: Accelerated training of rate-coded spiking networks. Not a chip runtime.

title: Lava-DL NetX
summary: Imports supported HDF5 network descriptions into connected Lava Processes.

title: Lava execution tutorial
summary: Distinguishes simulation and Loihi hardware execution configurations. ProcessModel placement determines where computation runs.

title: Sinabs and Speck deployment basics
summary: Torch conversion, DynapCNN mapping, discretization, device selection, and events in/out.

title: Deploying NIR models to Speck
summary: A specific NIR-to-Sinabs-to-device route. Tutorial adjusts neuron parameters to hardware-supported granularity.

title: snnTorch to Norse through NIR
summary: A software-to-software transfer with explicit time discretization, not a physical hardware benchmark.

title: snnTorch NIR export
summary: Exports supported computational graphs to NIR. Does not itself compile them to every chip.

title: NengoDL from TensorFlow
summary: Training a Nengo graph using TensorFlow, rather than exporting any arbitrary Keras model to any neuromorphic target.

title: NengoLoihi
summary: Loihi 1 backend based on NxSDK. Separate from the Lava / Loihi 2 stack.

title: sPyNNaker software framework
summary: PyNN-based model mapping and execution on SpiNNaker 1.

title: py-spinnaker2
summary: Distinct SpiNNaker 2 interface. PyNN-inspired is not the same as direct sPyNNaker compatibility.

title: Speck development kit manual
summary: Asynchronous convolution / IF / pooling cores, configurable membrane reset, and device operation.

title: Speck physical evaluation
summary: Physical converted-CNN and direct-training event-vision results. N-MNIST evidence is not the same workload as static-frame QCFS.

title: Speck event-driven neuromorphic system
summary: Physical event-vision platform evaluation. Single-event traversal latency is not whole-sample classification latency.

title: Efficient Video and Audio Processing with Loihi 2
summary: Physical Loihi 2 execution of Lava-DL models, including sigma–delta PilotNet. Host-streaming and on-chip input measurement boundaries differ.

title: Sigma-Delta Neural Network Conversion on Loihi 2
summary: Quantized ANN conversion with graded spikes and custom fixed-point microcode. Physical Loihi 2 evidence, not a stock binary-rate QCFS route.

title: Sigma-Delta Neural Network Conversion on Loihi 2, implementation manuscript
summary: nxkernel route, host preprocessing/readout, graded payloads, and fall-through versus pipelined execution.

title: Adaptive Fission: Post-training Encoding for Low-latency Spike Neural Networks
authors: Jiang, Y., Chen, F., Li, Y., Liu, Y., Gao, H., Zhang, T., Fang, Y.
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38
summary: QCFS-family spatial fission with physical Lynxi HP201 evaluation. Hybrid platform measurements do not isolate native sparse synaptic execution.

title: BIDL
summary: ANN and SNN layers, compilation, and execution on Lynxi platforms as well as CPU/GPU.

title: SpikingJelly inference on Lynxi
summary: Physical platform deployment example. A hardware interface is not proof of binary-event energy savings.

title: SpiNNaker neuromorphic system-on-chip
summary: Programmable ARM neuron simulation with a custom multicast spike router.

title: SpiNNaker 2 system architecture
summary: ARM processing elements, event communication, and numerical accelerators. Not a RISC-V platform.

title: SNN deployment on SpiNNaker 2
summary: snnTorch, NIR, and physical SpiNNaker 2 DVS-gesture deployment with quantized LIF models.

title: The BrainScaleS-2 accelerated neuromorphic system with hybrid plasticity
summary: Analog physical neuron dynamics with digital routing and processors. Analog ANN MAC mode must be distinguished from SNN operation.

title: Introduction to hxtorch.snn
summary: Differentiable SNN modeling and BrainScaleS-2 execution.

title: Convolutional networks for fast, energy-efficient neuromorphic computing
summary: Hardware-constrained convolutional inference on physical TrueNorth. Uses a binary representation rather than ordinary multi-step rate conversion.

title: Hardware evaluation of spike-based visual recognition
summary: Physical SpiNNaker and FPGA evidence for spiking deep belief networks. Not a converted CNN or QCFS validation.

title: PASCAL: Precise and Efficient ANN-SNN Conversion using Spike Accumulation and Adaptive Layerwise Activation
summary: Layer-wise temporal allocation with QCFS-related conversion. Accelerator timing study uses uniform T=4 and RTL/cycle estimates, not fabricated-silicon measurements.

title: LoAS
summary: Fully temporal-parallel accelerator design. A logical horizon can be spatially unrolled rather than executed as T serial hardware ticks.

title: PseudoSNN
summary: Heterogeneous timestep learning using pseudo-quantization noise. An allocation/training precedent, not a complete measured neuromorphic execution route.

title: Temporal Flexibility in Spiking Neural Networks: Towards Generalization Across Time Steps and Deployment Friendliness
authors: Kangrui Du, Yuhang Wu, Shikuang Deng, Shi Gu
summary: Mixed Time-step Training is the method inside Temporal Flexibility. Its Speck2e evaluation is timestep-free event-driven execution, not a clocked stage-horizon schedule.

title: SSNN
summary: Stage-wise timestep and boundary precedent from direct training. Real-valued temporal transforms require separate deployment treatment.

title: Differential coding for ANN-to-SNN conversion
summary: Differential representation is a distinct conversion direction. Do not equate every differential code with Loihi 2 graded sigma–delta microcode.

title: Quartz temporal conversion on Loihi
summary: Physical Loihi 1 temporal-coded CNN conversion. Architecture mapping and off-chip stages affect the measurement boundary.

title: Deep-Unrolling Multidimensional Harmonic Retrieval Algorithms on Neuromorphic Hardware
authors: V. C. Andrei, A. P. Drăguţoiu, G. Béna, M. Akl, Y. Li, M. Lohrmann, U. J. Mönich, H. Boche
venue: 2024 58th Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems, and Computers
summary: Complex-valued Few-Spikes conversion mapped to a physical single-chip SpiNNaker2 board with measured board power.

title: Hardware-Aware Fine-Tuning of Spiking Q-Networks on the SpiNNaker2 Neuromorphic Platform
authors: S. Arfa, B. Vogginger, C. Mayr
summary: Rate-coded, directly trained reinforcement-learning SNN with measured power, energy, and duration on physical SpiNNaker2.

title: When SNN Meets ANN: Error-Free ANN-to-SNN Conversion for Extreme Edge Efficiency
authors: G. Datta, Z. Liu, J. Diffenderfer, B. Kailkhura, P. A. Beerel
summary: The paper documents a Lava-DL route but does not identify a physical Loihi board, profiler, or on-chip measurement.
